relevance_reason: Reports GPI mutations in patients with GPI deficiency hemolytic anemia, with and without neurological dysfunction.

findings.statement: Kugler et al. (1998) studied 2 families with severe GPI deficiency. One patient (GPI Homburg) had nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia with additional neurological deficits, whereas 2 affected sibs in the second family (GPI Calden) showed no neurological symptoms.
quotes: we analysed DNA isolated from two patients with severe GPI deficiency, one of them with additional neurological deficits, and their families
In the second family studied, the two affected siblings showed no neurological symptoms.

findings.statement: In the neurologically affected patient with GPI deficiency (GPI Homburg), Kugler et al. (1998) identified compound heterozygosity for a 59A-C transversion resulting in a his20-to-pro (H20P) substitution and a 1016T-C transition resulting in a leu339-to-pro (L339P) substitution in the GPI gene. The authors suggested that insertion of proline was likely to affect folding and activity of the enzyme.
quotes: The neurologically affected patient (GPI Homburg) is compound heterozygous for a 59 A-->C (H20P) and a 1016 T-->C (L339P) exchange.
Owing to the insertion of proline, the H20P and L339P mutations are likely to affect the folding and activity of the enzyme.

findings.statement: In 2 sibs with severe GPI deficiency without neurological symptoms (GPI Calden), Kugler et al. (1998) identified 1166A-G (H389R) and 1549C-G (L517V) mutations in the GPI gene, located at the subunit interface.
quotes: The identified mutations are 1166 A-->G (H389R) and 1549 C-->G (L517V), which are located at the subunit interface.

findings.statement: Kugler et al. (1998) proposed that GPI mutations causing incorrect folding destroy both catalytic (GPI) and neurotrophic (neuroleukin) activities, leading to neurological symptoms (GPI Homburg), whereas alterations that allow correct folding retain neurotrophic properties (GPI Calden).
quotes: We propose that mutations that lead to incorrect folding destroy both catalytic (GPI) and neurotrophic (NLK) activities, thereby leading to the observed clinical symptoms (GPI Homburg).
Those alterations at the active site, however, that allow correct folding retain the neurotrophic properties of the molecule (GPI Calden).

relevance_reason: The title shows the paper reports DNA sequence abnormalities in human glucose 6-phosphate isomerase deficiency, which is the cause of CNSHA4. Only the title was available, so no specific variants or patient details can be extracted.

findings.statement: Walker et al. (1993) reported DNA sequence abnormalities in patients with human glucose 6-phosphate isomerase deficiency.
quotes: DNA sequence abnormalities in human glucose 6-phosphate isomerase deficiency.

relevance_reason: Describes mouse Gpi mutants with GPI deficiency and nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia as an animal model of the human disease.

findings.statement: Merkle and Pretsch (1993) described the first 2 mutations causing hereditary GPI deficiency with chronic nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia in a nonhuman mammal, the mouse. As in humans, the hemolytic syndrome (diminished erythrocyte number, lower hematocrit and hemoglobin, reticulocytosis, increased plasma bilirubin, and increased liver- and spleen-somatic indices) was manifested only in homozygous mutants; heterozygotes showed no hematologic or physiologic differences from wildtype.
quotes: The first two mutations causing hereditary glucose-6-phosphate isomerase (GPI) deficiency associated with chronic nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia in nonhuman mammals are described in the mouse.

As in humans, the hemolytic syndrome, which is characterized by a diminished erythrocyte number, lower hematocrit, lower hemoglobin, higher number of reticulocytes and plasma bilirubin concentration, as well as increased liver- and spleen-somatic indices, was exclusively manifested in homozygous mutants.

findings.statement: Merkle and Pretsch (1993) found that, allowing for the young erythrocyte population, homozygous mutant mouse erythrocytes had increased glucose-6-phosphate, normal or decreased glycolytic metabolites distal to the block, and apparently reduced ATP and glycolytic rate. Homozygous anemic mice showed hepatosplenomegaly, adaptations to hypoxia (elevated heart-somatic index and, in one line, lung-somatic index), and marked reduction of body weight and increased lethality correlated with the degree of tissue enzyme deficiency, which the authors attributed to reduced glycolytic capability of the whole organism.
quotes: homozygous mutant erythrocytes showed an increased concentration of glucose-6-phosphate and normal or decreased concentrations of glycolytic metabolites following the enzymatic block. The concentration of adenosine triphosphate and the glycolytic rate also appeared to be reduced.
these animals were characterized by a marked reduction of body weight and an increase of lethality both correlated with the degree of enzyme deficiency in tissues.

The latter findings were attributed to a reduced glycolytic capability of the whole organism caused by the enzyme defect in tissues, rather than representing secondary consequences of GPI deficiency in erythrocytes.

findings.statement: Merkle and Pretsch (1993) concluded that the similarity of physicochemical and kinetic properties of the mutant murine GPI proteins to human GPI-deficiency allozymes, and comparable metabolic and physiologic consequences, supported these mouse mutants as excellent models for human GPI deficiency.
quotes: support that these murine mutants are excellent animal models for the human disease.

relevance_reason: Case report describing a new GPI-deficiency variant (GPI Mount Scopus) causing nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia.

findings.statement: Shalev et al. (1993) reported GPI deficiency in a 23-year-old Ashkenazi Jewish man who showed the typical clinical course of the disorder: chronic hemolysis, which improved after splenectomy. The authors stated this was the first report of GPI deficiency in a patient of Jewish descent.
quotes: We recently diagnosed GPI deficiency in a 23-year-old Ashkenazi Jewish man who displayed the typical clinical course of this disorder.
is most often manifested by symptoms and signs of chronic hemolysis, ameliorated by splenectomy
this is the first report of GPI deficiency in a patient of Jewish descent

findings.statement: Shalev et al. (1993) found that the patient's GPI variant moved slowly on electrophoresis, showed only one of the two bands normally present, and was extremely thermolabile. They proposed naming it 'GPI Mount Scopus'.
quotes: The biophysical characteristics of the GPI variant are slow electrophoretic mobility, presence of only one of the two bands normally present, and extreme thermolability.
we propose to designate this enzyme variant "GPI Mount Scopus"

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal circulating enzyme concentration or activity

relevance_reason: Describes a patient with a GPI variant causing severe hemolytic anemia with neurologic features, and biochemical characterization of the stable mutant enzyme.

findings.statement: Zanella et al. (1980) described a new variant of glucosephosphate isomerase (GPI) associated with severe hemolytic anemia, mental retardation, and muscular hypotonia.
quotes: A new variant of glucosephosphate isomerase (GPI) associated with hemolytic anemia, mental retardation, and muscular hypotonia is described.

findings.statement: Zanella et al. (1980) found that the defective GPI enzyme showed increased affinity for fructose-6-phosphate, decreased affinity for glucose-6-phosphate, altered electrophoretic and isoelectrofocusing patterns, and a left shift of the precipitin curve, but was stable to heat, urea, guanidine-HCl, and storage. Optimum pH, Ki for 6-phosphogluconic acid and erythrose-4-phosphate, molecular weight, GPI-related antigen concentration, immunodiffusion pattern, and immunoinactivation were normal. The authors stated this was the first example of a stable mutant GPI associated with severe hemolytic anemia, enzyme instability having been present in all previously reported cases.
quotes: The defective enzyme showed increased affinity for fructose-6-phosphate (F-6-P), decreased affinity for glucose-6-phosphate (G-6-P) altered electrophoretic and isoelectrofocusing patterns, and shift to the left of the precipitin curve.
The enzyme was stable under all the conditions tested (heat, urea, guanidine-HCl, and storage).
This is the first example of the association of a stable mutant GPI with severe hemolytic anemia. Enzyme instability has been present in all previously reported cases.

relevance_reason: Describes a patient with GPI deficiency causing congenital nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia and characterizes a new enzyme variant (GPI Augsburg).

findings.statement: Arnold et al. (1980) reported a 1-year-old German boy, born to consanguineous parents, with chronic nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia and recurrent hemolytic crises caused by glucosephosphate isomerase (GPI) deficiency. Because of the parental consanguinity, the patient was considered a true homozygote.
quotes: In a 1-year-old German boy a GPI deficiency was found to be the cause of a chronic nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia with recurrent hemolytic crises.
Because of consanguinity of the parents, the patient is true homozygote.

findings.statement: Arnold et al. (1980) found that the deficient GPI enzyme in their patient had altered electrophoretic mobility, pronounced thermolability, increased affinity for glucose-6-phosphate and for the competitive inhibitor 6-phosphogluconate, and slightly changed pH optima for both substrates. Electrophoresis after freezing and thawing of the hemolysate suggested that the subunit alteration affected conversion of the main band into secondary bands; the authors designated the new variant GPI Augsburg.
quotes: The investigation of the biochemical properties of the deficient enzyme revealed an altered electrophoretic behavior, pronounced thermolability, an increased affinity for G6P, an increased affinity for the competitive inhibitor 6-PG, and slightly changed pH optima for both substrates.
Electrophoresis after freezing and thawing the hemolysate indicates that the genetic modification of the subunit involves the mechanism of transforming the main band into the secondary bands.
The properties of the new deficient GPI indicate a new variant designated GPI Augsburg.

relevance_reason: Case report of a boy with heterozygous GPI deficiency combined with hemizygous G6PD deficiency. The authors attributed the hemolysis to G6PD deficiency alone, so the paper relates to GPI deficiency only as a carrier observation.

findings.statement: Arnold et al. (1981) described a 5-year-old boy of Italian origin who had a severe hemolytic crisis. His hemolysate showed hemizygous glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency together with heterozygous glucosephosphate isomerase (GPI) deficiency. The authors concluded that only the G6PD deficiency seemed to be responsible for the hemolytic crisis. They noted that this was the fourth family reported with combined deficiency of these two enzymes, whose genes lie on different chromosomes.
quotes: A severe hemolytic crisis was observed in a 5-year-old boy of Italian origin.
Analysis of his hemolysate revealed a hemizygous deficiency of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) and a heterozygous deficiency of glucosephosphate isomerase (GPI).
Only the G6PD deficiency seems to be responsible for the hemolytic crisis.

findings.statement: Arnold et al. (1981) found heterozygous GPI deficiency and hemizygous G6PD deficiency in the red cells of an Italian boy. They reported that this was the fourth family in the literature with combined deficiency of these two enzymes.
quotes: Analysis of his hemolysate revealed a hemizygous deficiency of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) and a heterozygous deficiency of glucosephosphate isomerase (GPI).
According to the literature this is the fourth family with a combined deficiency of these two enzymes located on different chromosomes.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal erythrocyte enzyme concentration or activity

relevance_reason: Reports a patient with congenital nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia due to GPI deficiency and characterizes a new variant enzyme (GPI-Kaiserslautern).

findings.statement: Arnold et al. (1983) described a 13-year-old German girl with chronic nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia caused by GPI deficiency, with recurrent hemolytic crises that usually followed a febrile infection. She needed a blood transfusion during a crisis only once.
quotes: In a 13-year-old German girl a GPI deficiency was found to be the cause of a chronic nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia with recurrent hemolytic crises.
The hemolytic crises usually occurred after a feverish infection. Only once did the patient require blood transfusion during a crisis.

phenotypes.text: recurrent hemolytic crises after febrile infection

findings.statement: Arnold et al. (1983) concluded from family studies that their patient with GPI deficiency was doubly heterozygous for the deficiency.
quotes: Examination of the family indicated that the patient is doubly heterozygous for the deficiency.

findings.statement: Arnold et al. (1983) found that the deficient GPI enzyme in their patient showed altered electrophoretic migration, pronounced thermolability, increased affinity for glucose-6-phosphate, and slightly changed pH optima for both substrates. They designated it a new variant, GPI-Kaiserslautern.
quotes: The investigation of the biochemical properties of the deficient enzyme revealed an altered electrophoretic migration, a pronounced thermolability, an increased affinity for G-6-P and slightly changed pH optima for both substrates.
The described properties of the deficient GPI indicate that we are dealing with a new variant designated GPI-Kaiserlautern.

relevance_reason: The title reports defective hexosephosphate isomerization (glucose phosphate isomerase activity) in human red and white blood cells, which is the enzyme defect behind this entry. Only the title was available.

findings.statement: Paglia et al. (1969) reported that defective hexosephosphate isomerization occurred in both human erythrocytes and leukocytes.
quotes: Occurrence of defective hexosephosphate isomerization in human erythrocytes and leukocytes.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It shows the paper is about inherited variants of phosphohexose isomerase (glucose phosphate isomerase), the enzyme whose deficiency causes CNSHA4. No clinical, variant or numeric details can be extracted.

findings.statement: Detter et al. (1968) studied inherited variations in human phosphohexose isomerase (glucose phosphate isomerase).
quotes: Inherited variations in human phosphohexose isomerase.

relevance_reason: The title reports hereditary hemolytic anemia associated with GPI deficiency as a new red-cell enzyme defect, which is the subject of this entry.

findings.statement: Baughan et al. (1968) reported hereditary hemolytic anemia associated with glucosephosphate isomerase (GPI) deficiency, describing it as a new enzyme defect of human erythrocytes.
quotes: Hereditary hemolytic anemia associated with glucosephosphate isomerase (GPI) deficiency--a new enzyme defect of human erythrocytes.

relevance_reason: Title only; reports linkage of the glucosephosphate isomerase locus to the hemoglobin beta-chain locus in mice, which is comparative mapping context for the GPI gene rather than the human disorder.

findings.statement: Hutton (1969) used biochemical variants in mice to show linkage between the hemoglobin beta-chain locus and the glucosephosphate isomerase locus.
quotes: Linkage analyses using biochemical variants in mice. I. Linkage of the hemoglobin beta-chain and glucosephosphate isomerase loci.

relevance_reason: The title describes two new variants of glucose-phosphate-isomerase deficiency with hereditary nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia, which is the subject of this entry. Only the title was available.

findings.statement: Blume et al. (1972) characterized two new variants of glucose-phosphate-isomerase deficiency associated with hereditary nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia.
quotes: Characterization of two new variants of glucose-phosphate-isomerase deficiency with hereditary nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It describes a screening procedure for detecting glucose-phosphate isomerase deficiency, which is relevant to the diagnosis section of this entry.

findings.statement: Blume and Beutler (1972) described a screening procedure for detecting glucose-phosphate isomerase deficiency.
quotes: Detection of glucose-phosphate isomerase deficiency by a screening procedure.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It reports a glucosephosphate isomerase deficiency variant called GPI Elyria, which is relevant to CNSHA due to GPI deficiency, but no clinical or molecular details are given.

findings.statement: Beutler et al. (1974) reported glucosephosphate isomerase (GPI) deficiency due to a variant they named GPI Elyria.
quotes: Glucosephosphate-isomerase (GPI) deficiency: GPI elyria.

relevance_reason: Reports electrophoretic and kinetic studies of GPI in two Japanese families with GPI deficiency, the cause of CNSHA4. Only the title was available.

findings.statement: Nakashima et al. (1973) carried out electrophoretic and kinetic studies of glucosephosphate isomerase (GPI) in two unrelated Japanese families with GPI deficiency.
quotes: Electrophoretic and kinetic studies of glucosephosphate isomerase (GPI) in two different Japanese families with GPI deficiency.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It shows the paper is a review of hereditary glucosephosphate isomerase deficiency, which is this entry's disorder. No patient-level or variant data are available.

findings.statement: Paglia and Valentine (1974) reviewed hereditary glucosephosphate isomerase deficiency.
quotes: Hereditary glucosephosphate isomerase deficiency. A review.

relevance_reason: The paper describes 8 children from 2 families with hereditary nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia caused by glucose phosphate isomerase deficiency, including their clinical course, inheritance, and enzyme properties.

findings.statement: Hutton and Chilcote (1974) described 8 children (5 living, 3 deceased) from 2 families in Kentucky and Indiana with severe hereditary nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia caused by glucose phosphate isomerase deficiency. All affected children were severely anemic in early life. Three deaths occurred in young patients who did not receive adequate blood transfusions or whose parents refused to permit splenectomy. Growth and development were surprisingly normal, and no patient died of infection.
quotes: Eight children (5 living, 3 deceased) with severe hereditary nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia caused by glucose phosphate isomerase deficiency have been observed in two Kentucky and Indiana families.
All affected children were severely anemic in early life. Three deaths occurred in young patients who did not receive adequate transfusions of blood or whose parents refused to permit splenectomy.
Growth and development have been surprisingly normal and no patient has died of infection.

findings.statement: Hutton and Chilcote (1974) found that in patients with glucose phosphate isomerase deficiency, splenectomy generally abolished the requirement for blood transfusion, and no patient required regular transfusion after puberty.
quotes: Splenectomy generally abolishes the requirement for blood transfusion. No patient has required regular transfusion of blood after puberty.

findings.statement: Hutton and Chilcote (1974) concluded that the anemia due to glucose phosphate isomerase deficiency was expressed as an autosomal recessive trait, although the enzyme variant could be detected in hematologically normal heterozygotes.
quotes: The anemia is expressed as an autosomal recessive trait, but the enzyme variant can be detected in hematologically normal heterozygotes.

findings.statement: Hutton and Chilcote (1974) found that the abnormal glucose phosphate isomerase molecule was heat labile and was present in neutrophils and lymphocytes as well as in erythrocytes.
quotes: The abnormal isomerase molecule is heat labile and is contained in neutrophils and lymphocytes as well as in erythrocytes.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal erythrocyte enzyme concentration or activity

relevance_reason: Case report of GPI deficiency (GPI Homburg variant) causing congenital nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia with neuromuscular and granulocyte involvement.

findings.statement: Schröter et al. (1985) described a propositus with generalized glucosephosphate isomerase (GPI) deficiency who had a complex syndrome involving erythrocytes (congenital hemolytic anemia), granulocytes (decreased production of superoxide anion and reduced bactericidal activity in vitro), and the neuromuscular system (myopathy and mental retardation).
quotes: The propositus suffers from a complex syndrome involving erythrocytes (congenital haemolytic anaemia), granulocytes (decreased production of superoxide anion and reduced bactericidal activity in vitro) and the neuromuscular system (myopathy, mental retardation).

findings.statement: Schröter et al. (1985) characterized a new GPI variant, GPI Homburg, with very low specific activity in erythrocytes, granulocytes, and muscle tissue, nearly normal stability, normal kinetic properties, and decreased electrophoretic mobility.
quotes: A new glucosephosphate isomerase (GPI) variant is described which is characterised by very low specific activity in erythrocytes, granulocytes and muscle tissue, nearly normal stability, normal kinetic properties and a decreased electrophoretic mobility.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal erythrocyte enzyme concentration or activity

findings.statement: Schröter et al. (1985) suggested that the clinical syndrome resulted from generalized GPI deficiency due to decreased specific activity of the variant enzyme, which could not be compensated by increased de novo synthesis of GPI protein even in cells with active protein synthesis such as granulocytes and muscle cells.
quotes: It is suggested that the clinical syndrome results from generalised GPI deficiency due to a decreased specific activity of the variant enzyme, which cannot be compensated by an increase of de-novo synthesis of GPI protein even in cells exhibiting active protein synthesis such as granulocytes and muscle cells.

relevance_reason: The title says GPI deficiency can cause hydrops fetalis, which is part of the CNSHA4 phenotype. Only the title was available.

findings.statement: Ravindranath et al. (1987) reported glucose phosphate isomerase deficiency as a cause of hydrops fetalis.
quotes: Glucose phosphate isomerase deficiency as a cause of hydrops fetalis.

relevance_reason: Only the abstract was available. It describes an unstable, low-activity PGI (GPI) variant allele, PGI*3(Israel), in an inbred Israeli-Arab family. The authors suggested it was associated with severe anemia alongside AK and G6PD deficiencies.

findings.statement: Bonné-Tamir et al. (1987) studied phosphoglucose isomerase (PGI) and 16 other biochemical genetic markers in an inbred Israeli-Arab family that had previously been described with hereditary adenylate kinase (AK) and G6PD deficiency. They found a rare PGI*3 allele in 11 of 32 family members tested. Its electrophoretic mobility was similar to the PGI*3 allele found in Indian populations, but unlike the Indian allele it had very low specific activity and heat stability.
quotes: In this inbred family a rare PGI*3 allele was observed in 11 of 32 members tested, indicating an autosomal codominant inheritance.
The electrophoretic mobility of this allele is similar to that of the PGI*3 allele found in Indian populations, but unlike the Indian allele, it has a very low specific activity and heat stability.

findings.statement: Bonné-Tamir et al. (1987) concluded that the distribution of the PGI*3(Israel) allele (11 of 32 members tested) in an inbred Israeli-Arab family indicated autosomal codominant inheritance.
quotes: In this inbred family a rare PGI*3 allele was observed in 11 of 32 members tested, indicating an autosomal codominant inheritance.

findings.statement: Bonné-Tamir et al. (1987) designated the variant PGI*3(Israel) and suggested that it was a different, unstable mutation from the Indian PGI*3 allele. They also suggested that, together with the AK and G6PD deficiencies in the family, it seemed to be associated with severe anemia.
quotes: This PGI*3 allele, designated PGI*3 (Israel), seems to be a different unstable mutation and along with AK and G6PD deficiencies seems to be associated with severe anaemia.

relevance_reason: Reports a Mexican kindred with erythrocyte GPI deficiency (GPI Valle Hermoso), giving the biochemical characterization of a variant isozyme in a homozygous proband.

findings.statement: Paglia et al. (1975) studied a Mexican kindred with a unique erythrocyte glucosephosphate isomerase phenotype, which they called GPI Valle Hermoso. The proband's isozyme showed decreased activity and marked thermal instability. Its kinetics, pH optimum and starch gel electrophoretic pattern were normal.
quotes: Studies of a Mexican kindred present evidence for a unique phenotype of erythrocyte glucosephosphate isomerase, GPI Valle Hermoso.
an isozyme characterized by decreased activity, marked thermal instability, normal kinetics and pH optimum, and normal starch gel electrophoretic patterns

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal erythrocyte enzyme concentration or activity

findings.statement: Paglia et al. (1975) concluded that the proband was apparently homozygous for a mutant autosomal allele that governs production of the GPI Valle Hermoso isozyme.
quotes: The proband was apparently the homozygous recipient of a mutant autosomal allele governing production of an isozyme

findings.statement: Unlike in previously known cases, leukocyte and plasma GPI activities were unimpaired in the proband. Paglia et al. (1975) suggested that the structural alteration mainly made the enzyme unstable without greatly reducing its catalytic effectiveness, so that cells able to keep synthesizing protein could compensate. However, density-gradient fractionation of the affected erythrocytes did not show age-related losses of GPI.
quotes: Unlike previously known cases, leukocyte and plasma GPI activities were unimpaired.

This suggested that the structural alteration primarily induced enzyme instability without drastically curtailing catalytic effectiveness, thereby allowing compensation by cells capable of continued protein synthesis.
Age-related losses of GPI, however, were not evident by density-gradient fractionation of affected erythrocytes.

relevance_reason: This case report describes a patient with GPI deficiency (variant type Nijmegen) who had nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia caused by compound heterozygosity, and it covers family carrier studies.

findings.statement: Rotteveel et al. (1977) reported a patient from a Dutch family with glucosephosphate isomerase deficiency, type Nijmegen. The patient had nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia that presented in the neonatal period. The degree of hemolysis stayed about the same over the years, but trivial infections often triggered increased hemolysis that required blood transfusions.
quotes: This disorder decleares itself as a non-spherocytic hemolytic anemia, presenting in the neonatal period.
In the patient hemolysis was of the same degree during the years. However, trivial infections could often trigger an increase in hemolysis requiring treatment by blood transfusions.

phenotypes.text: infection-triggered increase in hemolysis requiring transfusions

findings.statement: Rotteveel et al. (1977) found on enzyme studies that the patient's GPI deficiency was caused by a double heterozygous state for two different GPI-deficient alleles. The parents and grandparents each carried one of these deficient alleles but showed no sign of hemolysis, such as shortened red-cell survival.
quotes: Enzyme studies revealed that the GPI deficiency in this patient was caused by a double heterozygous state for two different GPI deficient alleles.
The presence of one of these deficient alleles in the proband's parents and grandparents, was not accompanied by any sign of hemolysis, as for instance a shortened red-cell survival.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal erythrocyte enzyme concentration or activity

relevance_reason: Case report of congenital nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia caused by a new unstable GPI variant, with family studies pointing to compound heterozygosity.

findings.statement: Zanella et al. (1978) reported a patient with congenital nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia who had a new abnormal glucosephosphate isomerase (GPI), reduced glutathione (GSH) deficiency, GSH instability, and altered carbohydrate composition of the erythrocyte membrane.
quotes: A case of congenital nonspherocytic haemolytic anaemia associated with a new abnormal glucosephosphate isomerase (GPI), GSH (reduced glutathione) deficiency, and instability and altered carbohydrate membrane composition is reported.

findings.statement: Zanella et al. (1978) found that the only functional abnormality of the patient's mutant GPI appeared to be marked instability to heat, urea, and guanidine-HCl. Incubating normal and patient GPI with oxidizing and reducing agents suggested that the abnormality was in the SH groups of the mutant enzyme.
quotes: The only functional abnormality of the mutant enzyme seems to be a marked instability to heat, urea, and guanidine-HCl.
Experiments of incubation of normal GPI and the propositus's GPI with oxidizing and reducing agents seem to indicate that the abnormality resides in the SH groups of the mutant GPI.

findings.statement: Family studies by Zanella et al. (1978) suggested that the propositus was doubly heterozygous. One allele, from the mother, was a gene producing an inactive enzyme. The other, from the father, was a gene with a structural alteration that made the encoded GPI markedly labile.
quotes: Family studies suggest that the propositus is doubly heterozygous for a maternal gene producing an inactive enzyme and a paternal gene responsible for a structural alteration causing marked lability of the coded enzyme.

relevance_reason: Describes two new deficient GPI variants in homozygous patients with severe chronic hemolytic anemia, with biochemical characterization.

findings.statement: Kahn et al. (1978) described patients with severe chronic hemolytic anemia due to deficient glucose phosphate isomerase (GPI) variants. The patients' parents were consanguineous, and the patients were considered true homozygotes for the mutated GPI genes.
quotes: Two new deficient glucose-phosphate-isomerase (GPI) variants have been described in patients suffering from severe chronic hemolytic anemias.
The patients' parents were consanguineous, such that the patients were true homozygotes for the mutated GPI genes.

findings.statement: Kahn et al. (1978) found that in both GPI variants the main cause of the enzyme deficiency was molecular instability of the mutant GPI, with nearly normal catalytic activity. GPI 'Paris' showed slow electrophoretic migration and drastically altered substrate affinity (decreased for glucose-6-phosphate, increased for fructose-6-phosphate).
quotes: In both cases the main cause of the defect in enzyme activity was molecular instability of the mutated GPI molecules, their catalytic activity being nearly normal.

GPI 'Paris' was characterized by a slow electrophoretic migration and, above all, a drastically altered affinity for the substrates glucose-6-phosphate (decreased) and fructose-6-phosphate (increased).

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal erythrocyte enzyme concentration or activity

findings.statement: Kahn et al. (1978) characterized GPI 'Enfants malades', an unstable variant with slightly reduced electrophoretic mobility, an abnormal pH-activity curve, and an abnormal ratio of maximal velocity in the backward (fructose-6-phosphate to glucose-6-phosphate) versus forward direction.
quotes: GPI 'Enfants malades' exhibited a slightly reduced electrophoretic mobility, an abnormal curve of the activity in function of pH, and an abnormal ratio of maximal velocity in the backward direction

findings.statement: Kahn et al. (1978) could not prove a clear relation between the kinetic abnormalities of the mutant GPI variants and the metabolic changes of GPI-deficient red cells or the severity of hemolysis.
quotes: No clear relation could be proved between the kinetic abnormalities of the mutant GPI variants on the one hand and the metabolic changes of the GPI-deficient red cells and the severity of hemolysis on the other.

findings.statement: Kahn et al. (1978) emphasized a possible role of impairment of the hexose monophosphate pathway in the reduced viability of GPI-deficient red cells.
quotes: Finally we emphasized the possible role of the impairment of hexosemonophosphate pathway in the reduction of viability of the GPI-deficient red cells.

relevance_reason: Case report of GPI deficiency with mild hemolytic anemia describing a new variant (GPI-Mytho) with biochemical characterization and compound heterozygosity.

findings.statement: Galand et al. (1978) described a 6-year-old girl with glucosephosphate isomerase deficiency and mild hemolytic anemia.
quotes: A new case of glucosephosphate isomerase deficiency with mild haemolytic anaemia was observed in a 6-year-old girl.

findings.statement: Galand et al. (1978) found that the deficient GPI enzyme in their patient had profoundly decreased red cell activity, a normal electrophoretic phenotype, normal isoelectric point, normal optimum pH, molecular instability, and a clearly decreased Michaelis constant for fructose-6-phosphate.
quotes: Deficient enzyme was characterized by a profoundly decreased activity in the red cells, a normal electrophoretic phenotype, normal isoelectric point, normal optimum pH, a molecular instability and a clearly decreased Michaelis constant for fructose-6-phosphate.

phenotypes.text: profoundly decreased red cell glucosephosphate isomerase activity
phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal erythrocyte enzyme concentration or activity

findings.statement: Galand et al. (1978) concluded that their patient was a double (compound) heterozygote for a 'silent gene' inherited from the mother and an abnormal enzyme inherited from the father; because the paternal abnormal enzyme had undescribed characteristics, they proposed the name GPI-Mytho for this new variant.
quotes: Propositus was double heterozygote for a 'silent gene' inherited from the mother and an abnormal enzyme from the father.
Because this abnormal enzyme has undescribed characteristics, it responds to a new variant for which we propose the name GPI-MYTHO.

relevance_reason: Reports a family with GPI deficiency causing hydrops fetalis and severe hemolysis, with compound heterozygosity in the affected children, carrier parents, and prenatal diagnosis and treatment.

findings.statement: Whitelaw et al. (1979) reported the first child of unrelated, healthy Caucasian parents, who had GPI deficiency with severe hemolysis and hydrops fetalis and died at 3 hours of age.
quotes: Glucose phosphate isomerase (GPI) deficiency with severe haemolysis and hydrops fetalis was found in the first child of unrelated, healthy Caucasian parents. The child died at 3 hours.

findings.statement: Whitelaw et al. (1979) found that both parents of the affected child had 50% of normal red cell GPI activity, and qualitative studies of their red and white cells showed that each was heterozygous for a different GPI-deficiency variant allele; placental studies showed the propositus was a compound heterozygote.
quotes: Both parents were found to have 50% of normal red cell GPI activity and qualitative tests on their red cells and white cells showed that each was heterozygous for a different GPI variant allele associated with enzyme deficiency.
Tests on the placenta showed that the propositus was a 'compound' heterozygote.

findings.statement: Whitelaw et al. (1979) found that the healthy heterozygous parents each had 50% of normal red cell GPI activity.
quotes: Both parents were found to have 50% of normal red cell GPI activity

findings.statement: Whitelaw et al. (1979) made a prenatal diagnosis of GPI deficiency by studying amniotic cells obtained by amniocentesis at 28 weeks in the mother's second pregnancy; the second child was a compound heterozygote at the GPI locus, indistinguishable from the first.
quotes: Examination of amniotic cells obtained by amniocentesis on the mother at 28 weeks in her second pregnancy led to the prenatal diagnosis of GPI deficiency.
This second child, a 'compound' heterozygote at the GPI locus indistinguishable from the first

findings.statement: Whitelaw et al. (1979) reported that the prenatally diagnosed second affected child was successfully treated with immediate exchange transfusion and later blood transfusions.
quotes: was successfully treated by immediate exchange transfusion and subsequent blood transfusions.

relevance_reason: Reports a patient with congenital nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia due to a new GPI-deficient variant (GPI Roma), with characterization of the mutant enzyme.

findings.statement: Isacchi et al. (1979) described a 5-year-old Italian girl, born to first-cousin parents, with severe congenital hemolytic anemia and proven red cell glucose phosphate isomerase (GPI) deficiency.
quotes: In a 5-year-old Italian girl with severe congenital hemolytic anemia, red cell GPI deficiency was proven, and found to be due to a new variant, 'GPI Roma.'
The parents are first cousins and have been proven to be heterozygous for this variant.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal erythrocyte enzyme concentration or activity

findings.statement: Isacchi et al. (1979) found that the new variant, GPI Roma, was slightly heat-unstable and had a slightly increased Michaelis constant for fructose-6-phosphate. The patient's white cells showed a single predominant fast-migrating GPI form, whereas red cells showed this fast band plus a major band migrating as normal GPI and an additional slow band; the authors showed this could be ascribed to postsynthetic events modifying the charge of the mutant enzyme.
quotes: GPI Roma was slightly unstable to heat and exhibited a slightly increased Michaelis constant for fructose-6-phosphate.

A single predominant fast-migrating GPI form existed in the patient's white blood cells, while the electrophoretic pattern in the red cells was composed, in addition to this 'fast band,' of a major band migrating as normal GPI and of an additional slow band.
It is shown that this phenomenon may be ascribed to postsynthetic events modifying the charge of the mutant enzyme.

findings.statement: Isacchi et al. (1979) showed that both first-cousin parents of the affected girl were heterozygous for the GPI Roma variant, consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
quotes: The parents are first cousins and have been proven to be heterozygous for this variant.

relevance_reason: Review of GPI deficiency variants, clinical features, inheritance and pathomechanism of hemolysis.

findings.statement: Arnold (1979) reviewed glucosephosphate isomerase (GPI) deficiency, first reported in 1967, and noted that patients from all over the world suffer from a typical nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia with hemolytic crises during acute infections.
quotes: Since the first report of GPI deficiency in 1967 many patients from all over the world have been described.
The patients suffer from a typical nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia with hemolytic crises during acute infections.

findings.statement: Arnold (1979) stated that GPI deficiency is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait, with half of the patients being homozygotes and the others compound (double) heterozygotes.
quotes: The disease is inherited as an autosomal recessive, half of the patients are homozygotic, the others are double heterozygotes.

findings.statement: Arnold (1979) noted that the biochemical properties of the deficient GPI enzymes vary widely, so many well-characterized enzymes have been designated as different variants; alterations of physicochemical properties exceeded kinetic aberrations, and all defective variants were more or less unstable.
quotes: The biochemical properties of the deficient enzymes vary widely. Thus, many well characterized enzymes have been designated as different variants.
The modification of physicochemical properties surpasses kinetic aberrations. All defective variants are more or less unstable.

findings.statement: Arnold (1979) reported that GPI activity diminishes progressively in deficient red cells, leading to a rise in glucose-6-phosphate (G6P) concentration and, after in vitro aging, to dramatic impairment of glycolysis and concomitant hemolysis; the metabolic block was attributed to diminished GPI activity itself rather than inhibition of hexokinase by high G6P.
quotes: The activity diminishes progressively, leading to a rise in G6P concentration and in red cells after aging in vitro to a dramatic impairment of glycolysis and concomittant hemolysis.
The cause of the metabolic block is the diminished GPI activity itself and not an inhibition of hexokinase by the high G6P.

relevance_reason: Reports a new GPI-deficiency patient in a Dutch family, with biochemical characterisation of a new thermolabile variant (GPI-Utrecht).

findings.statement: Van Biervliet et al. (1975) described a new case of glucosephosphate isomerase deficiency in a Dutch family, with enzyme activity reduced to 20-25% of normal. The mutant enzyme was markedly thermolabile, losing 90% of its activity after 1 hour at 45 degrees C. Its pH optimum and electrophoretic migration were normal, and its Km for F-6-P and its Ki values for the competitive inhibitors 2,3-DPG and 6-PG were within the normal range. Because this variant differed from all known variants, the authors proposed naming it GPI-Utrecht.
quotes: A new case of glucosephosphate isomerase deficiency is described in a Dutch family. The activity of the enzyme was decreased to 20-25% of the normal value.
Characterization of the defect enzyme showed a pronounced thermolability. Heating of the enzyme at 45 degrees C showed a loss of activity of 90% after one hour.
The variant described here differs from all known variants. Therefore we propose to give to this new variant the name of GPI-Utrecht.

relevance_reason: The paper describes a new variant of glucosephosphate isomerase deficiency in a patient who appears to be a double (compound) heterozygote. This is the disorder covered by the CNSHA4 entry.

findings.statement: Van Biervliet et al. (1975) described a new variant of glucose-6-phosphate isomerase deficiency in a patient and studied the kinetics and properties of the enzyme. They compared their data with the other variants reported in the literature up to that time.
quotes: A new variant of glucose-6-phosphate isomerase deficiency is described. The enzyme kinetics and properties were studied.
These data are compared to the other variants described in the literature until now.

findings.statement: Van Biervliet et al. (1975) reported that genetic and electrophoretic data pointed to a double heterozygous state in their patient with glucosephosphate isomerase deficiency.
quotes: Genetic and electrophoretic data pointed to a double heterozygous state in the patient.
